                    ### Question
                    An investigator is studying the principles of cell-to-cell signaling of the autonomic nervous system. It is found that the adrenal medulla has receptors that, when activated, result in the immediate opening of Na+, Ca2+, and K+ channels, which subsequently leads to the secretion of epinephrine and norepinephrine. These receptors are structurally most similar to which of the following receptors?

                    ### Options
                    opa. H2 receptors of the stomach
opb. Alpha 1 receptors of the bladder neck
opc. M2 receptors of heart
opd. D2 receptors of the basal ganglia
ope. NM receptors of the quadriceps femoris muscle

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The receptors in the adrenal medulla, when activated, lead to the secretion of epinephrine and norepinephrine by opening Na+, Ca2+, and K+ channels. These receptors are structurally most similar to Alpha 1 receptors of the bladder neck.
